speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Prequantization and polarizations
summary: The actual heading on P000360 begins a five-page exposition of Kostant’s geometric quantization: symplectic and Hamiltonian vector fields, integral curvature, line bundles with connection, the prequantum representation, and polarized sections. The notebook’s factors of two and signs do not fit one convention throughout. The supplied catalogue span P000358--P000360 includes the end of the preceding year’s Perelomov discussion and omits most of this talk; those boundary pages are not new occurrences of record 229.

title: Academic-year heading
summary: This is the catalogue’s academic-year heading, retained as a record in its own right. The supplied range P000358--P000366 overlaps substantive records; no independent mathematical assertion is attached to the heading. P000365 is an ordering anchor before the 13 September talks, not a claim that its scan contains a separate handwritten year heading.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Springer resolution, flags, and Hall polynomials
summary: Gelfand describes Springer’s resolution of the unipotent variety and the geometry of invariant complete flags. The finite-field flag counts connect Hall polynomials with the even cohomology of flag varieties; a centralizer formula bounds the dimensions of Springer fibres. The literal claim about arbitrary reductive groups over every field needs geometric and characteristic qualifications.

speaker: B. I. Rosenfeld
title: Derivations of differential forms and an unidentified note by Rego
summary: The lower part of P000366 reports a note attributed to Rego in volume 272 of the Comptes rendus and recalls the Frölicher--Nijenhuis description of graded derivations. The named note and its proposed cohomology theory were not identified securely. The displayed calculus can nevertheless be reconstructed without inventing the missing result.

speaker: Vlastimil Pták
title: Critical exponents of finite-dimensional normed spaces
summary: The talk asks how many consecutive norm-preserving powers of a contraction force spectral radius one. It records exact Hilbert and polyhedral examples, a two-dimensional counterexample, questions about \(\ell_p^n\), the minimum over all norms, and a constrained spectral-radius extremum. A 1971 paper already answers the rational-\(p\) finiteness question more generally than the notebook acknowledges; the exact later fate of the other stated questions was not established.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: The affine Radon transform over a finite field
summary: Gelfand derives inversion by counting affine hyperplanes through one or two points and identifies a parallel-class range condition. A final remark connects finite-field subspace counts to Gaussian binomial coefficients and their \(q\to1\) limit. This heading precedes Kirillov’s P000369 heading despite the opposite order of catalogue record numbers.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Wavefront sets and oscillatory integrals
summary: The one-page talk introduces the wavefront set, conormal Lagrangians, pseudodifferential kernels, and oscillatory representations. Hörmander’s 1971 paper provides a close contemporary source. The notebook omits localization in its wavefront criterion and overstates the converse from wavefront containment to membership in a Lagrangian distribution class.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: The Godbillon–Vey class
summary: Bernstein explains the three-form attached to a cooriented codimension-one foliation, a homogeneous nonzero example, and the relation to formal vector-field cohomology. The claim of stability under deformation requires correction: arbitrary smooth families can change the Godbillon--Vey class. Atiyah’s talk starts later on the same page.

speaker: Michael Atiyah
title: Spectral flow and an index on a mapping torus
summary: Atiyah describes the integer obtained by following eigenvalues of a self-adjoint elliptic family and identifies it with the index of a suspended operator. A circle example, an eigenvalue-orbit argument, and remarks about diffeomorphisms and higher signatures follow. The main idea subsequently appeared in the third Atiyah--Patodi--Singer paper; the notebook’s derivative estimate and unitary conjugation sign need repair.

speaker: Pierre Deligne; translated by Yu. I. Manin
title: Motives: a two-line notice
summary: The entry says only that Deligne, with Manin translating, spoke about motives and the various cohomology theories of algebraic varieties. It records no theorem, construction, or conjecture sufficiently specific for a publication-level identification.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Schubert cells and invariant characteristic forms
summary: The talk compares the Schubert decomposition of a complex Grassmannian with invariant differential forms, curvature polynomials, and Schur functions. A separate intervention by I. M. Gelfand asks broadly about a defining-characteristic group algebra for \(SL_2(\mathbb F_q)\); the intended classification target is not specified. Vinogradov’s talk starts on the lower part of P000375.

speaker: A. M. Vinogradov
title: Differential operators as functors over a ring
summary: Vinogradov defines order by iterated commutators with multiplication and introduces the left and right module structures underlying jets, cojets, and higher derivations. His 1972 announcement gives the coherent version over a commutative unital ring. The notebook’s apparent permission to take an arbitrary noncommutative ring cannot be carried through unchanged.

speaker: A. M. Vinogradov
title: Jets, higher derivations, and algebraic differential complexes
summary: The second lecture develops universal jet modules, the recursive derivation functors, symbols, and de Rham and Spencer constructions. The characteristic-two discussion must distinguish skew symmetry from alternation. A literal example using only the prime field \(\mathbb F_2\) cannot support nonzero derivations; nearby dual-number and group-algebra examples are mathematically different.

speaker: A. M. Vinogradov
title: Six lemmas on differential operators and cojets
summary: The third lecture proves the elementary identities behind the differential-operator functors: pre- and post-composition, the first-order product identity, addition of orders under composition, and the universal evaluation/currying adjunction. These are the technical foundations of the 1972 announcement, with a commutative base ring understood.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Formal coordinate geometry and characteristic classes of foliations
summary: Gelfand develops the infinite frame bundle, its formal vector-field coframing, relative Lie algebra cohomology, and characteristic classes; Bernstein intervenes on inverse-limit manifolds. The final application is Bott’s obstruction to integrability, already discussed in the preceding year. The printed truncation threshold and the homogeneous degrees of Chern generators need correction. Arnold’s new heading begins later on P000394 and is excluded from this record.
